newsitem.title: USA: SBC wireless users grow 20.2 percent in yr.
newsitem.headline: SBC wireless users grow 20.2 percent in yr.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc on Tuesday said its cellular subscribers rose 20.2 percent in 1996 with the addition of 739,000 subscribers to make a total of 4.4 million.
The company reported an eight percent increase in earnings per share to $0.90 from $0.83 a year earlier.

The regional Bell said access lines to customers grew by 5.1 percent in 1996, with 14.5 percent of its customers now having an additional line. Southwestern Bell added 156,000 lines during the fourth quarter and 732,000 during the year.
Caller ID sales grew 37 percent during the year, SBC said.

"1996 was an excellent year for SBC from both a financial and a strategic perspective," said Chief Executive Edward Whitacre. He noted that the company added 1.9 million customers for long distance wireless services in 1996, one of many new services it plans to offer wireless users.
"Wireless is a particularly valuable business for us because it gives us access to a customer base with an above average appetite for telecommunication services," he said.
SBC expects to complete its merger with Pacific Telesis Group during the first quarter. (( Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
